Include a top-down tactical arena with the player, several enemies, walls and obstacles, visible patrol or path lines, detection cones, attack ranges, and distinct AI-state labels such as PATROL, ALERT, CHASE, and ATTACK. Add a compact inspector panel with player health and AI legend. Put strong emphasis on making tracking, pathfinding, and state transitions visually understandable while maintaining a cohesive, polished tactical identity.

history.critique: BRIEF/INTENT: The two most explicitly requested elements are missing or inert. (1) No patrol/path lines exist anywhere — enemies show only detection cones, yet the legend literally promises 'Waypoint sweep' and the brief demands visible path geometry; the tracking/pathfinding emphasis is therefore unmet. (2) No distinct attack-range rings are drawn, so 'detection cone' and 'attack range' are not visually separable as the brief requires. (3) State transitions are not demonstrated: all six units are frozen in PATROL, every legend count reads 0, THREATS=0 and the THREAT field is an empty dash, so the core 'state transition' goal is absent from the frame. CLARITY/HIERARCHY: A hard data bug — the legend shows PATROL count 0 while six PATROL enemies sit on the map — breaks trust in the whole readout. The player (the true focal subject) is a tiny cyan dot that loses to the green enemy markers, inverting the intended priority. The faint gray ring obstacles are ambiguous (wall? cover? decoration?) and clash with the bar/L wall language. The top-left SECTOR/MODE/THREAT overlay floats over the play area with a broken empty value. The HOSTILE UNITS list clips at E-04 of 6 with no visible scroll affordance. The one-off 'DETECTION CONE FOV 72° LOS 150m' tooltip on E-01 alone is inconsistent with the other labels. VISUAL CRAFT: Detection cones are flat low-opacity wedges whose straight FOV edges do not always read as emanating cleanly from the unit center, and the dashed arc is too faint to define the boundary; the scene is monochrome teal-on-black so the ALERT/CHASE/ATTACK hues in the legend never appear in-world, making the color system feel unfinished. Walls are flat with no depth cue. The hostile list and legend rows have dead space and a far-right zero column. EXPRESSIVENESS: Competent but generic dark-terminal HUD; the all-PATROL freeze removes any drama, trail, or 'memorable moment,' so the demo reads as a static map rather than a living behavior system. TRADE-OFF: Adding paths + attack rings + multiple live states to a dense grid risks clutter. The coherent resolution is a strict layered grammar (cone=vision, dashed ring=attack, dotted polyline+nodes=path, color ring+label=state) plus staging only 1-2 'hero' units in ALERT/CHASE/ATTACK so the legend colors and counts become true and the scene tells a transition story without overwhelming the six-unit field.
history.suggestion: Prioritized plan (preserves all required content, offline/self-contained): 1) FIX DATA TRUTH FIRST — drive legend counts, THREATS, and the THREAT field from live unit state so they match the map (no more 0-vs-6 contradiction, no empty dash); this is the cheapest, highest-trust win. 2) ADD THE MISSING GEOMETRY with a fixed visual grammar: patrol path = subtle dotted polyline with small waypoint nodes per unit; attack range = thin dashed circle in the unit's state hue, clearly distinct from the soft vision wedge; keep cone=vision only. 3) STAGE A TRANSITION NARRATIVE — promote 1-2 units to ALERT/CHASE/ATTACK so the legend's yellow/orange/red appear in-world and counts become non-zero; give the chasing unit a visible path/LOS line to the player so 'tracking' is literally drawn, leaving the rest in PATROL for contrast and to make the change legible. 4) REBALANCE FOCUS — enlarge the player into a distinct shape (triangle/diamond) with a soft pulse and a 'last-seen' tick when tracked, so it outranks the enemy dots as the focal point. 5) CRAFT PASS — give detection cones a radial gradient fill plus a brighter FOV edge for contrast; unify the ambiguous gray rings into the wall/cover language or label them; make enemy label placement consistent and move the FOV/LOS detail into the inspector on select instead of a one-off tooltip; fix the HOSTILE UNITS clipping with a proper scroll viewport or a compact 6-row layout. 6) IMPLY MOTION — add short motion trails/chevrons and a state-change flash ring so transitions read even in a still frame. Sequence 1→2→3 delivers the brief's core (paths, ranges, transitions) before 4-6 polish, keeping the cohesive tactical identity while making the system feel authored and alive.

I'll keep it as one prioritized plan in the suggestions field, and the critique field covering all four pressures with trade-offs.
